solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Amorous advance on Nancy’s very wrong (8)

blocks.note: Nancy is a French city, so its word for 'very' is très
to make a pass at someone

indicators.note: 'on' as in placed after: in an across clue, A on B puts B first, so TRES comes before PASS

annotation.surface: A flirtatious move in Nancy that goes badly wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: Nancy is not a woman here but the city in north-east France, which is why 'very' comes out in French.
annotation.definitionFit: An old sense of the noun: a trespass is a sin or wrong, as in the Lord's Prayer's 'forgive us our trespasses'.

entries.clue: Get up around noon and wash (5)

blocks.note: to get up is to rise
N is the standard abbreviation for noon

indicators.note: 'around' means encircling, so RISE is wrapped round N.

annotation.surface: A morning routine: get out of bed around midday and have a wash.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a lazy lie-in; really 'noon' just supplies N to sit inside RISE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rinse is to wash lightly in clean water, as with dishes or hair.

entries.clue: Magnificent carpet Lucas designed (11)

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: 'designed' means planned and laid out afresh, so the letters are arranged into a new pattern.

annotation.surface: A splendid rug from the workshop of a designer called Lucas.
annotation.walkthrough: Lucas is just a name that happens to supply the right letters alongside 'carpet'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something so grand or impressive it is a sight to behold.

entries.clue: China supporting vehicle manufacture using robotics (8)

blocks.note: an auto is a car
rhyming slang: china plate = mate

indicators.note: 'supporting' means holding up from below, so in a down clue MATE sits underneath AUTO.

annotation.surface: China's government backing a car industry that builds with robots.
annotation.walkthrough: China is not the country but Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with 'mate', so a china is a friend.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: to automate a process is to hand the manufacturing over to machines and robots.

entries.clue: Flag The King’s Speech as model of its kind? (8,7)

definitions.text: Speech as model of its kind

blocks.note: a standard is a flag or banner
the King's English is correct English

annotation.surface: Hailing the film The King's Speech as a model of its genre.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals pull toward the film about George VI; split it so 'The King's' is the English of the phrase 'the King's English'.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: Standard English is the form of the language held up as the model of correct speech.

entries.clue: Sitting back in MI6? Things here just the same (6)

blocks.note: sitting, as in having sat
MI6 is the Secret Intelligence Service, SIS

indicators.note: 'back' means backwards, so SAT is turned round to TAS.
'in' means located inside, so the reversed TAS is placed inside SIS.

annotation.surface: Asking whether anything ever changes at MI6, where everything stays the same.
annotation.walkthrough: MI6 is Britain's foreign intelligence agency, officially the Secret Intelligence Service.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: stasis is the condition in which nothing changes and everything stays just the same.

entries.clue: Some Aussies taking a nap (6)

blocks.note: the answer spans the end of 'Aussies' and the start of 'taking'

indicators.note: 'Some' means only a portion of, so just part of the letters of the phrase are used.

annotation.surface: A few Australians having a doze.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between 'Aussies' and 'taking'.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed word: siesta is Spanish for the short afternoon sleep, now used in English for any midday nap.

entries.clue: Cockney’s deceived count (3)

blocks.note: deceived = had; a Cockney drops the H, saying 'ad

indicators.note: a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, drops initial H, so 'had' in his mouth sounds like 'add'.

annotation.surface: A Londoner who has been conned over a count.
annotation.walkthrough: To be deceived is to be had; Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop the H.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to count up a column of figures is to add it.

entries.clue: Shy person’s opening mostly very tense (9)

blocks.note: an intro is an opening
VERY without its last letter
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: 'mostly' means for the most part, so most of the word is kept and its end dropped.

annotation.surface: A shy person is very tense at the start of any encounter.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': the shy person has the pieces that follow.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: psychology's term for someone turned inward, which everyday speech uses for a shy, reserved person.

entries.clue: Chuck out Austen novel (6)

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: novel as an adjective meaning new, so the letters take a fresh order.

annotation.surface: Throwing away a Jane Austen book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a noun about the book but is the adjective meaning new.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of removing from office: to throw out a politician or rider is to unseat them.

entries.clue: Amusing tale one acted out (8)

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: 'out' as in out of order or put out of place, so the letters are jumbled.

annotation.surface: A funny story that someone performed rather than just told.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Acted out' reads as one phrase, but 'acted' belongs to the fodder and 'out' is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a brief entertaining story about a real incident, usually told for laughs.

entries.clue: Get together with Moo, an otherworldly figure (4)

blocks.note: Moo is the setter, so the setter's name stands for ME
ET, the film's extra-terrestrial

annotation.surface: Meeting up with Moo, who turns out to be an alien.
annotation.walkthrough: Moo is the setter of this puzzle, so the name means ME.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: two people who arrange to meet for lunch come together.

entries.clue: Thought and time going into peacemaking attempt? (10)

blocks.note: mediation tries to make peace
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: 'going into' means entering, so T is placed inside MEDIATION.

annotation.surface: Wondering whether careful thought and time spent would make peace.
annotation.walkthrough: MEDIATION and MEDITATION differ by one T, which is what 'time going into' supplies.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: meditation is prolonged, serious thought on a subject.

entries.clue: What Socrates maybe did in his declining years? It’s inconsiderate (11)

definitions.text: What Socrates maybe did in his declining years

blocks.clueFragment: What Socrates maybe did in his declining years
blocks.note: a philosopher famous for thinking, doing less of it as he aged
careless of other people's feelings

annotation.surface: Speculating on the ageing Socrates, then calling that unkind.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as THOUGHT LESS: a philosopher's powers of thought fading as he aged.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: read as two words, a thinker who thought less in old age; as one, careless of others' feelings.

entries.clue: Trainer of English soldiers concealing old coin (8)

blocks.note: E for English
a ducat was an old European gold coin
OR = other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: 'concealing' means hiding within, so the soldiers' letters wrap round the coin.

annotation.surface: A drill sergeant training English troops who are hiding an antique coin.
annotation.walkthrough: A ducat was a gold coin used across Europe for centuries; 'other ranks' is the army term for soldiers who are not officers.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anyone who trains or teaches others is an educator.

entries.clue: Rescued, as Hannibal Lecter victim might have been? (9)

definitions.text: as Hannibal Lecter victim might have been

blocks.note: saved, as in 'deliver us from evil'

blocks.clueFragment: as Hannibal Lecter victim might have been
blocks.note: Lecter ate his victims' organs, so a victim might have had the liver removed

annotation.surface: Wondering whether one of Hannibal Lecter's victims could have been saved.
annotation.walkthrough: Hannibal Lecter, the cannibal of The Silence of the Lambs, boasts of eating a victim's liver, so the victim was de-livered.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: saved from harm, as in 'deliver us from evil'; and, split as DE-LIVERED, relieved of one's liver.

entries.clue: Sign captain’s on way back (4)

blocks.note: Captain Nemo of Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea

indicators.note: 'on way back' means returning, travelling in the reverse direction, so the name is read backwards.

annotation.surface: A portent that the ship's captain is heading home.
annotation.walkthrough: The captain is Jules Verne's Nemo, commander of the submarine Nautilus.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an omen is a sign foretelling what is to come.

entries.clue: A wet roof, slippery in wellies? (8)

definitions.note: wellies are one kind of footwear: the definition is by example

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: 'slippery' means sliding about, so the letters will not stay put.

annotation.surface: Clambering on a rain-soaked roof in rubber boots, and sliding.
annotation.walkthrough: Wellies (wellingtons) are rubber boots; the question mark flags a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: wellingtons are one kind of footwear, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Articles in Libération about Middle Eastern carrier (2,2)

blocks.note: la and le, the two French words for 'the'

indicators.note: 'about' as in turned about, facing the other way, so the letters are reversed.

annotation.surface: Newspaper pieces in the French daily Libération about an Israeli airline.
annotation.walkthrough: Libération is a French newspaper, which signals French articles; El Al is Israel's national airline.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: El Al is Israel's national airline, and a carrier is an airline.

entries.clue: Draw out Musk scandal? (8)

blocks.note: Elon Musk
-gate, the suffix for a scandal, from Watergate

annotation.surface: Prolonging a scandal about Elon Musk.
annotation.walkthrough: An Elon Musk scandal would be dubbed Elongate, since every scandal since Watergate gets the -gate suffix.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to draw out a piece of metal or wire is to stretch it longer.

entries.clue: One who’s unlike Iron Man? (6)

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a man is male

annotation.surface: Someone who is nothing like the superhero Iron Man.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals point at the Marvel superhero, but read as chemistry and plain English the name itself spells the answer, which is the one person the whole clue says is unlike him.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, a woman is the obvious person unlike any man, iron or otherwise, so the whole clue defines the answer.

entries.clue: Fat old vicar returned with cardinal (10)

blocks.note: O for old
the Rev, a vicar
W is short for with
a cardinal number, such as eight

indicators.note: 'returned' means sent back, so REV is turned back to VER.

annotation.surface: A portly elderly vicar coming back with a cardinal of the Church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman beside the vicar, but it is a cardinal number.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, overweight being the politer everyday word for carrying too much fat.

entries.clue: Half of Tory party makes a fuss (2-2)

blocks.note: the first half of TORY
a do is a party

indicators.note: 'Half of' means one of two equal parts, so only the first two of the four letters are kept.

annotation.surface: Half the Conservative Party kicking up a row.
annotation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party; 'party' then reads as a celebration, a do.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal British idiom: 'what a to-do!' means what a commotion or fuss.

entries.clue: Poet departs on steamer, heading north (5)

blocks.note: D for departs, as on a timetable
Etna, a volcano that steams

indicators.note: 'on' as in resting on top: in a down clue D sits above what follows.
'heading north' means travelling upwards, so in a down clue ETNA is read bottom to top.

annotation.surface: A poet leaving on a steamship bound northwards.
annotation.walkthrough: The steamer is not a boat but Mount Etna, the Sicilian volcano that gives off steam.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy, is one poet.

entries.clue: White Fiat car’s broken down (8)

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: 'broken down' means smashed into pieces, so the letters are broken up and reassembled.

annotation.surface: A white Fiat has broken down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'White' seems to describe the car's paint, but it is the definition: a white wine.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, with 'white' short for white wine: Frascati is a white from the hills near Rome.

entries.clue: Short fat girl (3)

blocks.note: SUET, cooking fat, minus its last letter

indicators.note: 'Short' means falling short or lacking a bit, so the word loses its final letter.

annotation.surface: A short, plump girl.
annotation.walkthrough: Suet is hard animal fat used in British puddings.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Sue, short for Susan, is one girl's name, and crosswords let 'girl' stand for any.

entries.clue: They go out theatrically (6)

blocks.note: reads like people leaving a room in a showy way
in the language of the theatre: a stage direction in a script

annotation.surface: People leaving in a showy, dramatic manner.
annotation.walkthrough: Exeunt is the Latin stage direction telling several actors to leave the stage.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal translation: exeunt is Latin for 'they go out', the phrase printed in play scripts.

entries.clue: Mad heretic carrying stick (6)

blocks.note: the letters run from the second letter of 'Mad' into 'heretic'

indicators.note: 'carrying' means holding inside, so the phrase holds the answer within its letters.

annotation.surface: A crazed heretic wielding a stick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a noun the heretic carries; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: glue adheres to paper, meaning it sticks to it.

entries.clue: Under pressure, ran to grab dope (8)

blocks.note: hared, ran fast like a hare
an ass is a fool

indicators.note: 'grab' means seize and hold, so HARED holds ASS inside it.

annotation.surface: Stressed out, someone rushes off to get hold of drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs; here it is a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone harassed is harried and flustered, feeling under pressure from all sides.
